solution.asked: Find literal count after maximal grouping.
steps: The four ON cells cover all combinations of B,C while A remains 0.
Those varying variables disappear from the group term.
The result Ā is one product with one literal.

hints: Identify the conditions under which four-cell k-map group applies.

question: The shown map has ON minterms 0 and 2 for variables A,B,C. What product covers exactly this adjacent pair?

solution.formula: m_0+m_2=\bar A\bar B\bar C+\bar AB\bar C=\bar A\bar C
steps: The first and last map columns are adjacent in Gray-code topology.
Between minterms 000 and 010 only B changes.
Drop B and retain ĀC̄, option C.
solution.explanation: Drop B and retain ĀC̄, option C.
commonMistakes: Map edges wrap around; a rectangular display does not remove their adjacency.

hints: Identify the conditions under which k-map edge adjacency applies.

question: For F(A,B,C)=Σm(0,1,3,7), which listed prime implicants are essential?

given: essential means covering an ON cell not covered by another prime implicant
steps: The prime terms are ĀB̄ (0,1), ĀC (1,3) and BC (3,7).
Minterm 0 is covered only by ĀB̄, and minterm 7 only by BC.
Thus A and C are essential. AC is not even an implicant because it includes OFF minterm 5.
solution.explanation: Thus A and C are essential. AC is not even an implicant because it includes OFF minterm 5.
commonMistakes: A large implicant is not automatically essential; unique coverage is the test.

hints: Identify the conditions under which essential prime implicants applies.
Start from $ \text{essential prime}\iff\text{uniquely covers an ON minterm} $.

verification.method: Enumerate prime cubes, build ON coverage chart and find unique-cover primes. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

solution.asked: Use allowed don’t-cares to enlarge a group.
solution.formula: F=C\quad\text{is valid on every specified cell}
steps: The two ON minterms and both don’t-cares all have C=1.
Assigning the don’t-cares high permits a four-cell group.
The single literal C covers it while all specified OFF cells have C=0.

commonMistakes: A don’t-care can be used if helpful; it is not a required ON cell.

question: Which K-map grouping rules are valid for ordinary two-level minimization?

options.text: Legal groups contain a power-of-two number of adjacent cells
Diagonal touching alone makes two cells adjacent
Groups may wrap across opposite map edges

solution.asked: Select valid adjacency and cover rules.
steps: Groups represent Boolean cubes, so their size is a power of two.
Overlap can help cover cells with fewer literals, and opposite edges are adjacent by Gray-code wrap.
Merely diagonal contact does not provide one-bit adjacency. Select A,C,D.
solution.explanation: Merely diagonal contact does not provide one-bit adjacency. Select A,C,D.
commonMistakes: A visually close diagonal is not a legal two-cell Boolean cube.

hints: Identify the conditions under which k-map geometry applies.
Start from $ g\in\{1,2,4,8,\ldots\} $.

verification.method: Boolean-cube topology: cardinality powers of two, one-bit adjacency and cyclic edges. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: For F(A,B,C)=Σm(0,2,5,7) with no don’t-cares, find the minimum total literal count of a two-level SOP.

solution.asked: Find the minimal sum of product literal counts.
steps: Minterms 0,2 form ĀC̄, and minterms 5,7 form AC.
No group can join these pairs without including an OFF cell, so two two-literal products are required.
Total literal count is 2+2=4.
commonMistakes: Count total literals across all products, not only the number of products.

hints: Identify the conditions under which minimal sop cover applies.
Start from $ F=\bar A\bar C+AC $.

verification.method: Exact global SOP literal minimization over all legal cubes and covers. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: For F=AB+ĀC implemented as two AND gates into an OR, a static-1 hazard can occur when A changes with B=C=1. How many additional product terms are sufficient for its standard hazard-free cover?

given: Two-level SOP with unequal gate delays
solution.asked: Find the number of needed consensus products.
solution.concept: Consensus coverage for a static hazard
steps: The ideal function stays 1, but delay mismatch can briefly make both original products zero.
The consensus term BC is independent of the changing input and remains high for the transition.
Adding that one product suffices for this stated static-1 hazard.
solution.explanation: Adding that one product suffices for this stated static-1 hazard.
commonMistakes: Logical redundancy can be useful for transition safety even though it does not change the truth table.

hints: Identify the conditions under which consensus coverage for a static hazard applies.
Start from $ AB+\bar AC\ \longrightarrow\ AB+\bar AC+BC $.

verification.method: One consensus cube covers both sides of the stated A transition; verify truth equivalence and transition-independent BC term. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: Which statements about don’t-care cells in minimization are correct?

options.text: They may be assigned 1 when that enlarges a useful ON group
They may instead be assigned 0 if that helps the chosen implementation
Every don’t-care must appear in the final ON cover
A specified OFF minterm cannot be treated as a don’t-care without changing the problem

solution.formula: F(x)\text{ is unconstrained only on declared don’t-care inputs}
steps: The output on a declared don’t-care input is not specified by the design requirements.
A minimizing implementation may use it as high or low; no rule forces its coverage.
Specified zero cells remain constraints. Select A,B,D.
solution.explanation: Specified zero cells remain constraints. Select A,B,D.
commonMistakes: Only explicitly declared unspecified cases may be assigned freely.

hints: Identify the conditions under which specified versus unspecified outputs applies.
Start from $ F(x)\text{ is unconstrained only on declared don’t-care inputs} $.

verification.method: Incomplete-specification semantics: enforce ON/OFF cells and leave only declared don’t-cares free. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.
